en: I bow to Vāk, the goddess of speech, to Sarasvatī who resides in the heart as consciousness; I always revere her who dwells in the throat, whose source is the lotus, and who is ever fond of the syllable Hrīṃ.
To the goddess who bestows intelligence, who grants boons, who fulfills all desires, who is the beloved of Keśava, who holds a lute in her hand, and who bestows boons; (2)
Aiṃ Hrīṃ! [I bow to her] who is fond of mantras, the destroyer of evil intellect, self-luminous, without support, and the remover of the darkness of ignorance.
I bow to the beloved of the Jinas, who bestows liberation, who is eternally constant, who grants excellent boons, who delights in purification, and who is merged within the solar orb. || 4 ||
"O Goddess who possesses the form of knowledge, who is the lamp of the world, and who destroys the bonds of devotees"—thus was the Goddess perfectly praised by the high-souled Vāgīśa. (5)
She revealed herself, possessing a radiance like that of the autumnal moon.
"O venerable one, choose a boon—whatever dwells in your heart. (6)
"If the Goddess is pleased with me, let divine knowledge be bestowed.
Those men who always praise me with devotion by means of this hymn, || 7 ||
They obtain supreme knowledge equal to my own prowess, as well as poetic skill through my grace and likewise abundant fame. (8)
That man who, having become purified, recites this hymn at the three junctions of the day, I shall always dwell upon his throat; of this there is no doubt.
Oṃ aiṃ vāgvādini mama jihvāyāṃ eeṃ hrīṃ mantrasarasvati svāhā.
The Śrīvāgvāṇīstotra composed by Bṛhaspati is complete.
